//: Non-secret behaviour. Secrets live in .env. Keys starting with // are comments.
//server: port: left out on purpose. Under Docker set PORT in .env instead, so the
compose port mapping cannot drift from the app. Environment wins over
this file and a mismatch is warned about at startup.
configPollMs: how often this file is re-read, default 10000. Everything
under jira and backup below applies without a restart; port and vaultDir
do not, and a change to those is reported as ignored rather than faked.

//jql: The only thing that decides what exists in the vault. Anything this
query returns gets a note; anything it stops returning has its note
Types are excluded rather than listed so that projects with renamed or
localised subtask types are still included.
jira.jql: assignee = currentUser() AND issuetype not in (Epic, Story) AND status in ("In Progress", "In Review") ORDER BY updated DESC
jira.//targetSubdir: Where notes live, relative to the vault root. Owned by the sync.
jira.//taskContext: TaskNotes context. This is what the Work tasks base filters on.
//statusMap: Jira status name on the left, TaskNotes status id on the right.
Looked up case insensitively. Anything absent uses defaultStatus.
Your TaskNotes config currently defines only none, open, in-progress
and done, which is why several Jira statuses collapse onto
in-progress below. Add an 'in-review' status in TaskNotes settings and
change the mapping here to tell them apart in the task list.
The true Jira status is always written to the note's jiraStatus field,
jira.//defaultStatus: Used for a Jira status not in statusMap. Logged once as a warning.
jira.//reconcileCron: Safety net behind the webhook, because webhooks get dropped.

backup.//endpoint: Cloudflare R2: https://<account-id>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com. null for real AWS.

//: Only for the raw encrypted backup artifact. Credentials stay in .env.
Use the same URL the LiveSync plugin uses. A public domain needs no
Docker network setup at all, which is why it is the default here.
